newsitem.title: INDIA: India's CMIE sees 96/97 sugar output down at 15 mt.
newsitem.headline: India's CMIE sees 96/97 sugar output down at 15 mt.

text.p: India's sugar production in 1996/97 (October-September) is expected fall to around 15 million tonnes from 16.5 million in the previous year, the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE) said.

In its October review of the Indian economy released on Wednesday, the Bombay-based independent think-tank said the projected fall in sugar production in 1996/97 was mainly due to a 3.0 percent decline in sugarcane output during the year.
"But the lower production in 1996/97 is still one million tonnes or 7.0 percent higher than the 14.0 million consumed, including exports, during 1995/96," the CMIE said.
It said the government's decision to allow free exports of sugar in August had not yet been implemented and hinted at reports of lobbying in sugar industry for and against the move.
The CMIE did not give details.
